rejectedClasses: excess depth, nodes, properties, enums, or byte size

proved: Unsafe or unsupported schema keywords such as pattern, $ref, and oneOf fail before native disclosure, credential access, or provider transmission.
Rust validates complete normalized arguments against the exact function definition included in the approved request and returns valid, invalid, or missing-definition status.
The frontend independently preflights schemas and validates streaming proposals with pinned AJV 2020 settings that do not coerce, remove, or default data.
One cross-language harness feeds the same valid, invalid, and unknown-function fixtures through the native loopback runtime and the frontend validator; both report the same three statuses.
Diagnostics contain at most eight bounded path/keyword codes and exclude argument values in the adversarial fixtures.
Every native and frontend validation result reports domainStatus unreviewed and executable false, including schema-valid proposals.
The product displays schema pending/matches/mismatch/definition-missing separately from domain review and offers no Run tool control.
The content-free run record omits response, argument, and diagnostic bodies while its output hash commits to proposal and validation state.
No validator or UI path gained MCP, Drive, filesystem, plugin, editor, network, or shared-project mutation authority.
notProved: Tool-specific semantic or domain validation, safety, truth, usefulness, authorization, or user intent.
Tool execution, result transmission, multi-turn continuation, retry, idempotency, side-effect classification, or permission brokering.
Complete JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 support; the surface intentionally accepts only the documented safe subset.
Live OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or xAI request/response behavior, provider policy, billing, rate limits, or server-side tools.
Packaged native Send once dialog interaction or a shipped updater artifact containing this checkpoint.
Any model-quality, feature-parity, or superiority property.
